# Expected values for the builder (docs/rules/construction.md), captured from the original program in the emulator (ADR 0008):
# tools/GhidraDump/emulate.py, the verb construct (remove with the phase routine 0x42965c at the last phase of each cycle), run to the
# passes the scenarios name. The click b@x,y,T places the site of the type T at the pass AT.
# A checkpoint line "pass=N phase=P ..." gives, as the emulator left them after the pass N, the generator words (rng), the 16 bytes of a
# settler (s<slot>: slot 14 is the castle's builder, slot 3 the settler without a job the second request takes), the 18 bytes of a
# building item (b<slot>, 14 bytes once the building stands: the original keeps a pointer to the flag item there), and the request
# bytes 0x42 to 0x45 of its flag (f<slot>). The flag and building slots are one higher than the engine's (the dummies of the tables);
# the settler slots are the same.
# A line "pass=N fill<slot>+=NN" gives the growth of byte 8 of a building item that the engine does not model: the castle's hand-out
# (+01, a good on the way) and the delivery at the building (+0F, the good on site). The engine's hand-out lays a good on the castle's
# flag at once where the original's first settler carries it out about 130 passes later (docs/rules/construction-materials.md), so the
# test empties the castle of planks and stones, keeps the draw the hand-out takes, and adds these amounts to the site's fill at the passes
# the original did. The builder's turns, blows, figures (the draw of each), and ticks are the engine's own.
# Not production code: no routine of the program is transcribed here, only values the program produced.

# The scenarios end before the worker's own work, which the slices of the buildings' types port: the forester's start routine (job 8)
# is not in the engine, so the generator after the worker's entry would differ.

# The two sites of builder-two-sites with no hammer in the stock (the click k@17,0 writes the stock word of the good 17 to 0 before the
# sites are placed, and k@17,1 gives it one hammer before the pass 300). The castle's builder takes the forester's site; the second site's
# request finds a settler without a job and no hammer, so it fails: the site's status byte 5 takes bit 2 (0x04), the retry scan clears it
# the next pass, and the site asks again at its next turn, 33 passes later. Once the hammer is there the request makes the settler of the
# slot 3 a builder (0x80, a worker on the way), and the stock word falls to 0. The lines stop at that pass: the original's castle settler
# then stands on the castle's flag with a good of the hand-out until the pass 345, so the new builder waits in the castle until the pass
# 348, where the engine's hand-out lays its goods at once and he steps out at the pass 332 (docs/rules/construction-materials.md).
# builder-no-hammer construct:1:1234,5678,9ABC:25:15,5:18,6;15,9:16,6,00;16,6,2223::40:420:k@17,0;b@17,5,9;b@14,8,2;300=k@17,1

# A second site while the castle holds no settler without a job. Five roads leave the castle's flag (the roads of split-nofree-1000 in
# road-splits.txt), and their carriers take the five settlers without a job: the last (slot 1) leaves at the pass 164. The castle's builder
# takes the forester's site at 19,5; the woodcutter's site at 15,9 asks for a builder at each of its turns, and its request fails: the
# site's status byte 5 takes bit 2 (0x04), the retry scan clears it the next pass, and the site asks again 33 passes later. Before the
# pass 164 the request also fails at the passes where the castle's list of settlers without a job is empty (a settler enters it at his
# turn); from the pass 197 on, the castle holds none. The castle's goods still go out to both sites (fill), and the game goes on. A pass
